requirements.statement: Each status message that indicates the progress of a process is contained in an element that takes the log, progressbar or status role, or an accepted equivalent.

citations.quote: Chaque message de statut qui indique la progression d’un processus utilise-t-il l’un des attributs WAI-ARIA `role="log"`, `role="progressbar"` ou `role="status"` ?

routes.statement: The element containing the message has role="log", role="progressbar" or role="status".

citations.quote: Soit utilise l’un des attributs WAI-ARIA `role=”log”`, `role=”progressbar”` ou `role=”status”` ;

routes.statement: The element containing the message has aria-live="polite", standing for the log role when that is the intent.

citations.quote: Soit utilise l’attribut WAI-ARIA `aria-live=”polite”` si l’intention est de signaler l’équivalent d’un `rôle “log”` ;
Un attribut WAI-ARIA `aria-live="polite"` associé à un message de statut peut valoir pour un rôle WAI-ARIA `log` ;

routes.statement: The element containing the message has aria-live="polite" and aria-atomic="true", standing for the status role when that is the intent.

citations.quote: Soit utilise les attributs WAI-ARIA `aria-live=”polite”` et aria-atomic=”true si l’intention est de signaler l’équivalent d’un rôle “status”.

requirements.statement: A progress status message shown graphically as a progress bar has an explicit progressbar role; the live-region equivalents do not stand for it.

citations.quote: Dans le cas d’un message de statut indiquant la progression d’un processus et matérialisé graphiquement par une barre de progression, un rôle WAI-ARIA `progressbar` explicite est nécessaire.

routes.statement: The element representing the progress bar has an explicit WAI-ARIA progressbar role.

citations.quote: un rôle WAI-ARIA `progressbar` explicite est nécessaire.

rationale.text: The methodology is the one of test 7.5.1, whose fifth step covers this test. The first requirement has three routes: one of the roles log, progressbar or status; aria-live="polite" standing for log; or aria-live="polite" with aria-atomic="true" standing for status. The technical note adds a second requirement for a progress message drawn as a progress bar: an explicit progressbar role is then necessary. Whether content is a status message indicating progress, whether it is drawn as a progress bar, and which role the author intends a live region to stand for, are judgment. Whether a native progress element, whose role is implicit, meets the note's word explicit is not said. Progress messages also appear only while a process runs, after the user starts it. So the candidate is none and no check is linked. No axe rule is tagged for this test; axe's aria-progressbar-name checks that a progressbar has a name, which this test does not ask. Applicability is judgment: whether the page shows progress messages is not known from the page as loaded. Needs is state, since progress follows an action.
